input: Look into becoming a licensed notary public

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Notary requirements — application steps, fees, exams, bond requirements, and appointing authority — vary significantly by U.S. state or country, making location the single biggest determinant of the entire plan.

The user said 'look into,' which could mean just researching requirements, or actively completing every step to get licensed. Knowing how far they want to go shapes whether this is a research task or an action plan.
Whether this is for personal use, a current employer, or to run an independent notary business changes the urgency, the type of commission needed, and any additional certifications worth pursuing.

Some states require an exam, a training course, a surety bond, and filing fees totaling hundreds of dollars. Knowing the user's budget and available time affects which steps to prioritize or whether costs are a barrier.
Some notaries work exclusively in-person; others want Remote Online Notarization (RON) authorization, which involves additional tech requirements and state-specific rules — a major fork in the path.
The user may want a checklist, a step-by-step action plan, links to official resources, or a timeline. Knowing their preferred output format determines how to structure the plan.

Success could mean simply understanding the requirements, submitting an application, or being fully commissioned and ready to notarize documents. Clarifying the end goal prevents under- or over-planning.

gold.taskDescription: The user wants to explore and pursue the process of obtaining a notary public license.

questions.title: Which U.S. state (or country) are you located in?
questions.description: Notary laws, application processes, fees, and requirements are entirely state- or country-specific. This is the most critical piece of information needed to make the plan accurate.

questions.title: Do you want to research requirements, or actively complete the process?
questions.description: Determines whether this is an information-gathering task or a full step-by-step action plan leading to an actual commission.

questions.title: Is this for personal use, an employer, or your own notary business?
questions.description: The intended purpose affects which commission type to pursue, whether an Employer Identification Number is needed, and whether additional credentials like a Notary Signing Agent certification are relevant.

questions.title: Do you have a budget in mind for fees, bonds, and training?
questions.description: Costs can range from under $50 to several hundred dollars depending on the state. Knowing the budget helps flag any financial barriers early and prioritize low-cost steps first.

questions.title: Do you want to perform notarizations in-person, remotely online, or both?
questions.description: Remote Online Notarization (RON) requires separate authorization in most states and additional technology setup, making this a major fork in the plan.

questions.title: What format would be most useful — checklist, timeline, or narrative guide?
questions.description: Shapes how the resulting plan is structured and presented so it is immediately actionable for the user.

questions.title: What does success look like — understanding requirements, or commission in hand?
questions.description: Clarifies the finish line: is the goal to know what is involved, to submit an application, or to be fully commissioned and actively notarizing documents?
